sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Knocknarea is an Irish mythological site. It rises as a high mountain above the town of Sligo. Some six thousand years ago builders laid a mound and raised a rock cairn on its top. Legend says this cairn, called Miosgan Meabha or Mebh's lump, guards the grave of Medb of Cruachan. Yet medieval texts report a different builder. They say Eogan Bel, the last pre-Christian king of Connacht, made the cairn. They also state that Medb fell far away on the shore of Lough Ree along the Shannon. Local custom in Sligo asks visitors to the summit to add a stone to the cairn. Taking stones from it is held to bring very bad luck.
